key_insight: Plant-on-a-Disc (POD) is a radial microfluidic phytofluidic platform that lets researchers grow and analyze eight seedlings in parallel under controlled flow while preserving in situ, multimodal root-shoot measurements.
engineering_relevance: By combining uniform hydrodynamic delivery with low-shear creeping flow in a compact PDMS device, POD offers a practical tool for studying how transport and confinement jointly shape root physiology.
method: Cost-effective PDMS fabrication using a wire-drawing technique
Radial microchannels feeding a central sump beneath a shared optical window
Sequential bright-field, fluorescence, and Raman imaging with one microscope objective
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dimensionless transport analysis, finite-element modeling, and Brassica experiments showing accelerated root elongation, ROS generation, anisotropic cortical cell expansion, and Raman-detected carotenoid signatures under flow.
watch_item: The platform’s utility may depend on careful calibration of flow and shear to avoid perturbing root development or biasing comparisons across channels.
paper_title: Plant-On-a-Disc (POD): A Phytofluidic platform enabling In Situ Root Analysis
